source_name: IFC Ukraine country programme page (ERA / $2bn package)
why_relevant: Pointer to the shape of IFC's Ukraine pipeline, including the Economic Resilience Action programme and its stated pivot toward digital infrastructure — useful for anticipating which advisory disclosures will appear next.

source_name: World Bank Group donor financing mechanisms for Ukraine (URTF/PEACE trust funds)
why_relevant: Explains which trust funds finance which Ukrainian operations, which is the key to knowing whose procurement rules apply and where the resulting notices will be published.

source_name: EIB project procurement and technical assistance calls
why_relevant: EIB publishes its own TA calls (confirmed Ukraine-relevant examples: microfinance operations TA covering Ukraine/Moldova/Georgia, and TA supporting the Ukraine Recovery Programme). Loan-financed contracts by promoters are published on TED. Together these expose EIB-funded financial-infrastructure work and its consultants.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU-financed external action and IFI-linked notices)
why_relevant: EU external-action service contracts for Ukraine (technical assistance to the financial sector, EU4Digital-type facilities) and EIB-financed promoter contracts are published here with award notices naming the winning consortium. Machine-readable and covers awards, not just calls.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal — Ukraine opportunities
why_relevant: Central EU entry point for calls and tenders open to Ukraine, including digital-economy facilities. Identifies EU-funded programme vehicles before any national announcement.

source_name: EU4Business in Ukraine — programme and project directory
why_relevant: Ukrainian-language hub listing 40+ EU-funded SME/access-to-finance projects with implementing partners (GIZ, EBRD, banks). Pointer to the partner banks and implementing agencies that then run their own supplier procurement.

source_name: EU4DigitalUA — EU digitalisation project in Ukraine
why_relevant: Successor to EGOV4UKRAINE; covers state digital infrastructure, e-services, data protection and cybersecurity. Indirect for banking, but its interoperability, e-ID and data-exchange components are prerequisites that payment and banking vendors build against, and its supplier ecosystem overlaps.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — donor-project pages (USAID Financial Sector Reform, IBR)
why_relevant: The beneficiary regulator's own description of donor-funded programmes touching payment infrastructure and financial-sector strategy, naming donors (USAID, IFC, SECO) and workstreams. Highest-authority statement of what donor money is actually buying at the NBU.

source_name: Ministry of Economy / Cabinet of Ministers register of international technical assistance (МТД) projects, incl. ProAID portal and open-data dataset
why_relevant: Ukrainian law requires state registration of every donor technical-assistance project; the register lists donor, implementer, beneficiary, budget and — critically — the attached procurement plans (плани закупівель). This is the single best Ukrainian-side cross-reference for donor-funded banking/payments work, including projects that never surface on IFI portals in an obvious form.

source_name: Prozorro donor-procurement module (закупівлі міжнародних донорів)
why_relevant: Since 2023 a dedicated Prozorro module runs tenders under donor rules (World Bank recommends its use for the recovery portfolio; USAID, WB and ICRC contracts already run through it). Where donor-funded IT procurement is routed here it becomes fully machine-readable via the Prozorro API — a rare case of IFI money with open structured award data.

source_name: UNDP Ukraine tender announcements + UNDP global Procurement Notices / UNGM
why_relevant: UNDP is a major implementing agency for EU and bilateral donor money in Ukraine and procures IT systems and advisory services directly; notices carry ITB/RFP references and are mirrored on UNGM. Reaches donor-funded digital work that is neither IFI-loan nor Prozorro.

source_name: USAID Office of Inspector General / GAO reports on Ukraine awards
why_relevant: Audits of costs incurred by USAID awardees implementing Ukraine activities, and GAO reviews of supplemental funding, name implementers and describe activity scope and spend — a way to reconstruct vendor/implementer landscapes when the programme pages themselves are thin, and one that survives programme-page takedowns.

source_name: USAspending.gov — US federal award data for Ukraine financial-sector activities
why_relevant: Authoritative, machine-readable record of US-funded contracts and cooperative agreements including recipient name, obligated amounts, place of performance Ukraine and NAICS/PSC codes — the definitive way to identify who actually implements USAID financial-sector and payments programmes.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — aggregated donor tender and award notices
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that mirrors and archives IFI/EU/USAID tender and award notices, including Ukraine-relevant ones (confirmed listings for EU4Digital Facility Phase III covering Ukraine and awarded USAID Ukraine contracts). Useful as a cross-check and as a historical archive when primary portals rotate notices off.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — EBRD cooperation page and financial sector strategy documents
why_relevant: Sovereign-side accounting of EBRD portfolio volume and project count in Ukraine, plus the Financial Sector Development Strategy that donor programmes are written against. Provides the Ukrainian-language framing and official project counts to sanity-check IFI-side disclosures.

source_name: Ukrainian institutional relays of IFI consultant tenders (SPFU, Ukraine Reform Support Fund, Ukrinform ЄБРР tag)
why_relevant: Ukrainian beneficiary institutions and media announce IFI consultant tenders in Ukrainian, often earlier and with more contextual detail than the English portal entry, and sometimes for assignments not easily findable on ECEPP. Confirmed pattern: SPFU relaying an EBRD consultant tender; the Reform Support Fund relaying an EBRD consultant search for reform delivery teams.

source_name: EBRD Ukraine procurement briefing deck hosted by Prozorro Infobox
why_relevant: A 2025 EBRD briefing on project procurement and opportunities in Ukraine — explains the current notice channels, thresholds and pipeline framing straight from the Bank, which is the methodological key to collecting the rest of this cell correctly.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — Open Banking hub (bank.gov.ua/payments/open-banking)
why_relevant: Regulator's own landing page for the open-banking programme: concept, NBU Board Resolution No. 80 of 25.07.2025 (Regulation on Open Banking), API standard documents, compliance deadlines (1 Jan 2026) and programme milestones. Primary dated anchor for the whole procurement wave in this cell.

source_name: NBU SEP pages (Система електронних платежів / instant payments)
why_relevant: Official pages on SEP-4.x, the migration to SEP-4.1 (instant credit transfer live from 01.12.2024) and the participant onboarding schedule. Participant lists and rollout schedules are the trigger for core-banking/payment-hub vendor work at every bank.

source_name: le.bank.gov.ua — NBU legal/normative portal (resolutions on payment services and open banking)
why_relevant: NBU's legal-acts mirror where the binding texts (Положення про відкритий банкінг, authorisation rules) and their amendment history live. Dated regulatory changes let you time procurement waves rather than guess at them.

source_name: zakon.rada.gov.ua — Ukrainian legislation portal (Law on Payment Services; NBU authorisation regulations)
why_relevant: Canonical text of the authorisation regulation for non-financial payment service providers and of the Law 'Про платіжні послуги' (No. 1591-IX) whose open-banking provisions took effect 01.08.2025. Defines which actor categories exist, hence which vendor categories get bought.

source_name: Open API Hub (OAH) — oah.com.ua
why_relevant: Ukrainian open-banking solution vendor/hub co-founded by the EMA association and GD Next, selling API Connect (AISP/PISP connector) and API Kit (ASPSP-side modules). Its own site names partner banks — Sense Bank, Credit Agricole Ukraine, Oschadbank, OTP Bank, MTB Bank — i.e. a directly published vendor-to-bank win list.

source_name: Ukrainian Processing Center (UPC) — open banking platform / API aggregation
why_relevant: UPC is the incumbent Ukrainian processor, registered with the NBU as a technology operator, and runs an Open Banking Platform / Open API Marketplace built with Tietoevry Banking on Berlin Group NextGenPSD2. It is simultaneously a competitor, an aggregator and a channel through which banks buy open-banking connectivity.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking newsroom — Ukraine open banking releases
why_relevant: Foreign-vendor newsroom is where Ukrainian selections get announced with dates and named counterparties — here UPC choosing Tietoevry for its open-banking platform. Vendor newsrooms are usually earlier and more explicit than the bank's own comms.

source_name: Salt Edge blog / Ukraine open-banking compliance materials
why_relevant: Salt Edge is a major international open-banking compliance/aggregation vendor courting the Ukrainian market, co-running webinars with local core-banking vendor CS (Chernihiv-based CS Ltd). Webinar co-branding reliably reveals distribution partnerships before contracts are announced.

source_name: PrivatBank Open Banking developer portal (API for third-party providers)
why_relevant: PrivatBank is one of the first two institutions (with PUMB) authorised in Q1 2026 for payment-initiation and account-information services. Its developer portal publishes API docs, planned maintenance and API availability/performance statistics — a rare, quantitative window on an ASPSP's actual implementation and its underlying stack.

source_name: Bank open-banking / Open API pages (ASPSP developer pages across Ukrainian banks) — e.g. Alliance Bank
source_subtype: bank Open API landing pages (source class)
why_relevant: Every ASPSP must publish an Open API page by the compliance deadline. Collected as a class (Privat, PUMB, Raiffeisen, Universal/monobank, Oschadbank, OTP, Sense, Credit Agricole, MTB, Alliance, Ukrgasbank...), these pages reveal per-bank standard choice, gateway/consent vendor and go-live dates — a synchronised procurement census.

source_name: Diia integration portal (integration.diia.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Official technical portal for integrating Diia services (Document Sharing, Дія.Підпис, Antibot, Validation) into third-party platforms, including banks. Documents the integration modes, and Mintsifra publishes counts of integrated banks (e.g. ~48 banks using sharing, ~21 using Дія.Підпис) plus the 2025 paid-tariff model for banks. Directly identifies state-rail integration and the integrator partners around it.
